title: The widow's jar (1 Kings 17:8–16)
hookLine: a starving widow shares her last cake, and the flour doesn't run out

cards: A woman is picking up sticks at the gate of a town called Zarephath. Two sticks, the text says. Enough for one small fire.

The brook has dried up, and the word has come to Elijah: go to Zarephath, "behold, I have commanded a widow woman there to sustain thee." The ravens were commanded. Now it's a widow, and she doesn't seem to know it.

Zarephath isn't in Israel. It belongs to Zidon, the country Queen Jezebel comes from. Elijah, a stranger and a foreigner, asks her for a little water, and then, as she turns to get it, a piece of bread.

teach.h: A HANDFUL OF MEAL, AND DIE.
teach.b: Her answer, in the King James Bible, is stark: "As the LORD thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die."
One small word: thy God. Not mine. Yours.
She is not of Elijah's people, and she expects this to be the last meal she and her son will eat.
Elijah says something that sounds outrageous: "Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first."

teach.h: AS THE LORD THY GOD LIVETH.
teach.b: Then the promise: "The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the LORD sendeth rain upon the earth."

teach.h: MAKE ME A LITTLE CAKE FIRST.
teach.b: And the text says it plainly: she went and did according to the saying of Elijah. She gives from her last, to a foreigner, on the strength of a promise from a God she calls his.
And "the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail." The text never says the barrel overflowed. The meal simply doesn't run out: "she, and he, and her house, did eat many days."

teach.h: ENOUGH, EACH DAY, UNTIL THE RAIN.
teach.b: Enough, not more. In Luke's Gospel, Jesus remembers her: there were many widows in Israel in that famine, but Elijah was sent to none of them except this one, a widow in Sarepta, a city of Sidon.

how: Some Christians tell the story of the widow of Zarephath when they talk about generosity in hard times, and Jesus's mention of her in Luke 4 is sometimes read alongside it.

games.why: she went and did according to the saying of Elijah, and the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail.

practice: Name something you don't have much of right now, time, money, patience, energy, and notice how tightly you're holding it.
Then picture one person who could use a small piece of it, not all of it, a handful: a phone call, a meal, an hour, a kind word. If you pray, you can bring that person before God.

orig.note: Hebrew: a jar or pitcher; the King James calls it a barrel of meal (1 Kings 17:12).

carryVoice: Your line: the jar did not fail. A handful of meal, shared first, and it lasted. Day seven hundred thirty-one, done.
